_readme: Team data structure v3 (obligation-first). Values are illustrative unless marked REAL. REAL examples come from UN R103 0.3.0 and UN R128 0.11.0 as seen in the PDFs. Keys starting with an underscore are notes, not data.
_big_idea: A paragraph is where an obligation is written down. An obligation is what the grader matches (one-to-one, same scope, condition and constraint) and what the engineer reads. So: paragraphs (clauses) are kept as verbatim EVIDENCE, and obligations are the UNIT we search, match, output and compare across versions.

_layers.layer_1_sources: Verbatim PDF content as a tree of clauses with pages. Built by code (rules), no model needed. Same for every regulation.
_layers.layer_2_obligations: Atomic, self-contained obligations extracted from clauses by a model, each pointing back to its clauses. Built once per regulation, cached, measurable against the dev expected.json.
_layers.layer_3_matching: Product parts matched to obligations, with verdict + reason + evidence. Accepted matches become the submission requirements.

_design_rules: 1. Clause text is verbatim (only whitespace normalised). Obligation text is our rewrite, and always points back to the clause that proves it.

2. One obligation = one subject + one modality (shall / shall_not / may) + one condition + one constraint. Split when constraints differ. Keep together when it is one constraint with several values (a range or a table). This is the granularity the grader uses.
3. Ids are stable and readable. clause_id = <REG with _>@<version_label>:<label>, e.g. UN_R103@0.3.0:5.1.3. obligation_id = clause_id + #n of the primary clause.
4. Two kinds of links in one flat structure: parent_id = the tree (one parent), refs and supports = the graph (any number).
5. lineage_key lets us line up the same clause or obligation across versions: <regulation>|<label> (+ #n for obligations). Sub-goal = compare obligations with the same lineage_key.
6. Every decision (regulation in or out, obligation accepted or rejected) stores evidence: clause_id + page + exact quote. A script checks the quote against the clause text.
7. Embeddings and indexes are derived data in separate files keyed by id, never mixed into the source JSON, so the parser can be re-run on any new PDF without losing work.

_files_layout.data/clauses/<REG>@<version>.jsonl: one clause per line, one file per PDF (parser output, re-runnable on any PDF)
_files_layout.data/obligations/<REG>@<version>.jsonl: one obligation per line, one file per PDF (model output, cached)
_files_layout.data/derived/: embeddings and keyword indexes keyed by clause_id and obligation_id
_files_layout.runs/<case_id>/submission.json: requirements wrapped in team_id and case_id, README format. Extra fields are allowed and ignored by the platform. Check with tools/validate.py.

regulations.title: <take from regulations/index.json>

scope.text: This Regulation applies to LED light sources shown in Annex 1 and intended for use in approved lamps of power-driven vehicles and of their trailers.
scope._note: REAL scope text (R128 page 1). vehicle_categories only when stated, else null. A hint, never a hard filter (scopes contain exclusions, e.g. R132 excludes vehicles approved under R83).

regulations._note: refers_to / referred_from are computed from clause refs.

versions._note: used_for_main follows the partner rule (latest if it exists, otherwise base). Both versions are parsed because the sub-goal needs them.

clauses.text: The installation of the replacement pollution control device shall be at the exact position of the original pollution control device, and the position on the exhaust line of the oxygen probe(s) and other sensors, if applicable, shall not be modified.
clauses._note: REAL (R103 page 4). 'label' is the string that goes into source.paragraph (annex clauses look like 'Annex 8 2.1'). section_kind: scope | definition | administrative | requirement | test_procedure | transitional | annex_data | informative.

heading_path: 3.12. LED substitute light sources - additional requirements
clauses.text: The correlated colour temperature of LED substitute light sources emitting white light shall be no more than 3000 K, unless an appropriate keying is defined in the relevant data sheet of Annex 1 for light sources with a specified higher correlated colour temperature.
clauses._note: REAL (R128 page 8). A clause with a condition, a constraint and an exception, and a reference to an annex. Cross-references to regulations outside regulations/index.json get in_index=false (set by script): we may only cite regulations in the index.

clauses.text: Moreover, in the case of LED light sources emitting white light, the minimum red content of the light shall be such that:
parse_warnings: the limit is in a formula image, not in the text
clauses._note: REAL (R128 page 5). Shows why images matter later: the actual constraint (k_red at least 0.05) lives in the formula image. Images are skipped for now, so has_unparsed_image=true marks where a vision model is needed later.

obligations.text: The replacement pollution control device shall be installed at the exact position of the original pollution control device.
obligations._note: REAL clause, obligation written by hand as a format example. The clause holds TWO obligations, so it gets two entries (#1 and #2).

obligations.text: The position on the exhaust line of the oxygen probe(s) and other sensors shall not be modified, if applicable.

subject.item: oxygen probe(s) and other sensors on the exhaust line

obligations.text: The correlated colour temperature of an LED substitute light source emitting white light shall be no more than 3000 K, unless the relevant data sheet in Annex 1 defines an appropriate keying for a higher specified correlated colour temperature.

subject.item: LED substitute light source emitting white light

obligations.exception: an appropriate keying is defined in the Annex 1 data sheet for a higher correlated colour temperature

verification.test_case_hint: measure correlated colour temperature of the white-light source

obligations._note: REAL clause, hand-written obligation. addressee values: product | manufacturer | applicant | authority | technical_service. Obligations addressed to the authority or the applicant are usually administrative; check the dev expected.json to see which ones count.

parts.name: Rear position lamp
parts.function: Makes the vehicle visible from behind
parts.search_text: rear position lamp, light signalling, luminous intensity on reference axis

evidence.note: ILLUSTRATIVE, from the challenge brief example

parts._note: search_text is what gets embedded and keyword-searched against obligations.

regulation_decisions.reason: Scope covers replacement pollution control devices for exhaust systems, which a rear lamp is not.

evidence.quote: This Regulation applies to the type-approval, as separate technical units, of pollution control device to be fitted in one or more types of motor vehicles

regulation_decisions._note: REAL quote (R103 page 1). Verdicts: applies | maybe | not_applicable. Recall matters, so 'maybe' goes forward and is cleared later.

matches.reason: ILLUSTRATIVE. The obligation sets the intensity range for rear position lamps.
ILLUSTRATIVE. Concerns LED substitute light sources. Only relevant if the lamp uses an exchangeable LED source. Kept for the engineer to confirm or discard.
matches._note: Rejected and review matches are kept with a reason. This is the proof for what we left out. Verdicts: accept | review | reject.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall give 4 to 17 cd on the reference axis.
requirements.why: R148 covers rear position lamps; this obligation gives the intensity range for P-01.
requirements._note: id, text, source and test_case are the README format. source is filled from the primary clause (regulation, version, page_start, label). The other fields are ours and ignored by the platform. Page and paragraph here are placeholders.

version_diff._note: ILLUSTRATIVE. status: unchanged | modified | removed | added. Default alignment by lineage_key (same label); a model or a person fixes renumbered clauses. Derived data.

changes._note: README sub-goal format. requirement_id must exist in requirements_old.json for modified/removed and be null for added. Built from version_diff.

links._note: All links are ids inside the flat lists above. No separate graph store is needed.
links.refers_to: clause.refs[] (clause or regulation to clause or regulation)
